title: No idempotency key on createWorkout/createExercise: a lost HTTP response duplicates the workout/exercise (and its sets) on reconnect replay
description: syncOne creates server-side records with non-idempotent POSTs and only writes its checkpoint (server_workout_id / server_exercise_ids_by_local) AFTER the await resolves. createWorkout (line 188-195) and createExercise (line 201-226) send plain POSTs via api.ts (createWorkout api.ts:93-108, createExercise api.ts:154-170) with no Idempotency-Key / client-id header anywhere in the codebase (grep for idempoten/client-id returns nothing). If the request reaches the Rust backend and the row is committed, but the response is lost before it arrives (TCP drop the instant connectivity flaps back — exactly when the online handler fires syncPendingSessions), the await rejects with a fetch TypeError, isNetworkFailure() catches it in syncPendingSessions (actions/sync.ts:69-74) and setOffline() is called with the checkpoint never written. On the next 'online' event syncOne re-runs createWorkout/createExercise from scratch and creates a SECOND workout (or second exercise with a fresh replaceSets), so the user's logged session is silently duplicated on the server.
attackOrTrigger: Fully-offline session (negative id) with pending edits. Connectivity flaps back, window 'online' fires syncPendingSessions -> syncOne -> createWorkout POST commits server-side but the connection drops before the 201 returns. isNetworkFailure() true -> record stays, server_workout_id still undefined. Next reconnect re-runs createWorkout -> duplicate workout. Same path for createExercise mid-loop -> duplicate exercise carrying a duplicated replaceSets set list.
why: Replay is at-least-once with no server-side dedup handle from the client, so any lost response on the two non-idempotent creates duplicates a user's logged workout data. replaceSets (PUT, full replace) and endExercise/endWorkout are naturally idempotent, so the gap is specifically the two POST creates.
fixSketch: Generate a stable client-side idempotency token per offline entity (e.g. derived from the negative local id) and send it as an Idempotency-Key header on createWorkout/createExercise so the backend can dedup a retried create; or have the backend return the existing row for a duplicate token. Persist the token in the offline record so it stays stable across retries.

verdicts.title: No idempotency key on createWorkout/createExercise: a lost HTTP response duplicates the workout/exercise (and its sets) on reconnect replay
verdicts.reason: Confirmed in offline.ts: workoutId/exerciseMap are only persisted via checkpoint() after the api.createWorkout/api.createExercise await resolves (lines 187-196, 198-227). There is no idempotency-key/client-id parameter passed to either call, and no guard elsewhere in syncOne that would detect a duplicate on replay. If the awaited promise rejects (network drop) after the server has already committed the row, workoutId/exerciseId remain unset and the next syncOne invocation re-enters the `if (!workoutId)` / `if (!exerciseId)` branches and re-creates. The mechanism as described is real and reachable in this source.

verdicts.title: No idempotency key on createWorkout/createExercise: a lost HTTP response duplicates the workout/exercise (and its sets) on reconnect replay
verdicts.reason: Code at lines 187-227 matches the claim exactly: workoutId/exerciseId are only persisted via checkpoint() after the await resolves, and there is no idempotency key or client-generated id sent with createWorkout/createExercise. The reachability lens finds no guard blocking this: syncOne is invoked from the 'online' handler in syncPendingSessions with no in-flight lock preventing a second sync run after a network drop, and a request-committed-but-response-lost scenario is a normal, well-known TCP/HTTP failure mode (not a contrived edge case), especially plausible at the exact moment connectivity is flapping back (the trigger condition). The offline record (negative session id, pending edits) is reachable via any fully-offline workout session, and the online/offline transition is a real browser event this code explicitly listens for. Nothing here contradicts reachability.

verdicts.title: No idempotency key on createWorkout/createExercise: a lost HTTP response duplicates the workout/exercise (and its sets) on reconnect replay
verdicts.reason: Read offline.ts:163-267 directly. The only mitigation present is the checkpoint() helper, and its own comment (lines 175-177) states its purpose is to avoid re-running createWorkout/createExercise on retry — but checkpoint() is invoked only AFTER each await resolves (line 195 after createWorkout, line 226 after createExercise). There is no idempotency-key/client-id header in the request construction, no try/catch around the awaits, and no dedup mechanism on the client side at all. If the awaited fetch throws (e.g. TypeError from a dropped connection) after the server has already committed the row, workoutId/exerciseId remain unset and the checkpoint is never written, so the existing guard does not cover exactly the window the finding describes. Nothing in this file makes the scenario unreachable or recoverable — the described gap is real and un-mitigated from an already-mitigated-lens reading of this code.

title: refreshFromBackend deletes an offline record with unsynced edits when the server session was completed elsewhere, silently dropping the local edits
description: In the no-active-server-workout branch, when an offline in_progress record maps to a server workout id (server_workout_id, positive), refreshFromBackend checks isAlreadyCompleted = offlineSessionId > 0 && workouts.some(w => w.id === offlineSessionId) and, if true, calls deleteOfflineSession(offlineInProgress.key) and clears currentSession. That offline record only exists because it carries unsynced local edits. If the server-started session was ENDED on another device, it now appears in the workouts list as a completed (non-active) workout, so isAlreadyCompleted is true and the record — including sets/edits logged offline that were never pushed — is deleted without ever calling syncOne. The offline edits are lost with no notice.
attackOrTrigger: Start a workout on device A (server session id 5, active). Device A goes offline and logs more sets -> offline in_progress record for session 5 with server_workout_id=5. The same session is ended on device B. Device A reconnects: refreshFromBackend finds no active workout, offlineSessionId=5 is present in workouts (now completed) -> isAlreadyCompleted -> deleteOfflineSession -> the offline sets are discarded, never synced.
why: The heuristic 'server workout id is in the list => already synced/completed' conflates 'completed on server' with 'local edits already pushed'. The record can be present precisely because edits are still pending, so deletion is silent data loss under a multi-device end sequence.
fixSketch: Before deleting, push the pending edits (run syncOne / replaceSets against the completed workout) or surface a conflict notice instead of unconditionally deleting; only delete when the record has no unsynced deltas beyond what the server already holds.

verdicts.title: refreshFromBackend deletes an offline record with unsynced edits when the server session was completed elsewhere, silently dropping the local edits
verdicts.reason: Matches the code exactly at backend.ts:56-68: when there is no active server workout, offlineInProgress is looked up, isAlreadyCompleted is computed purely from `offlineSessionId > 0 && workouts.some(w => w.id === offlineSessionId)`, and on true it calls deleteOfflineSession(offlineInProgress.key) directly — no call to syncOne, no check of pending edits/sets beyond presence in the completed workouts list. No guard distinguishes 'completed and already synced' from 'completed elsewhere while local edits are still pending'. The claimed data loss path is real as written.

title: submitEndSession online path: a mid-flight network failure in the endExercise Promise.all loses the selected mood/feedback and leaves the workout un-ended
description: When ending a session while online, submitEndSession fires endExercise for every not-done exercise via Promise.all (line 309-328), then endWorkout (line 330-334). On a network failure partway through the Promise.all, some exercises are ended server-side, endWorkout is never called, and the catch (line 345-349) treats it as offline: it calls persistInProgressSession(state), which saves the record with status 'in_progress' and does NOT carry end_mood or end_notes (offline.ts:89-110). The user-selected mood/feedback and end notes captured in the end modal are dropped. On reconnect syncOne re-ends the exercises but, because the record is in_progress with no end_mood, it never calls endWorkout (offline.ts:269) and then deletes the positive-id record (offline.ts:283-285). The workout is left active on the server with the mood/feedback lost.
attackOrTrigger: Online, tap End Workout, pick a mood + notes. Connection drops during the parallel endExercise calls. isNetworkFailure -> persistInProgressSession saves in_progress WITHOUT end_mood. Reconnect syncs exercises, skips endWorkout, deletes record. refreshFromBackend re-shows the still-active session; the chosen mood/feedback is gone and the user must re-end.
why: The end-of-session mutation is not treated as a single queued 'pending_sync' unit on the online failure path (unlike the offline branch at line 291-301 which correctly stores end_mood/end_notes), so the completion intent and feedback are silently lost. Recoverable only because the session reappears active, but the logged mood/notes are gone.
fixSketch: In the online submitEndSession catch, persist a pending_sync record carrying end_mood/end_notes (mirror the offline branch) instead of calling persistInProgressSession, so syncOne finishes the endWorkout with the captured feedback on reconnect.

verdicts.title: submitEndSession online path: a mid-flight network failure in the endExercise Promise.all loses the selected mood/feedback and leaves the workout un-ended
verdicts.reason: Confirmed at session.ts:308-349: the online path runs Promise.all over endExercise calls, then endWorkout; the catch block (345-349) on isNetworkFailure calls persistInProgressSession(state) with no `extra` argument, so per persistInProgressSession's implementation (offline.ts:89-110) the resulting record has status 'in_progress' and no end_mood/end_notes fields set (unlike the offline branch at 291-301 which explicitly builds a 'pending_sync' record carrying end_mood/end_notes). The mood/notes captured in local state (state.endMood/state.endNotes) are never persisted on this path, matching the claim.
